# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the bomb for the first time. Let me record everything carefully.

**What I observe:**
- DISPLAY shows the number **1**
- LIGHT is **orange**
- Seven wires, in order: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see all of this but cannot hear, cannot read the manual, cannot touch the bomb. My speech reaches Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute.

Blind can touch the bomb and work its parts, but sees nothing — so Blind needs me to describe colours and markings in words. Mute reads the manual but cannot speak — Mute needs to get the rule to Blind somehow. The chain is: I describe the bomb to Blind (and Mute), Mute reads the rule and must convey it — but Mute can't speak. Mute can gesture to me... but I can't see gestures? No wait — I'm Deaf, I can see. Let me recheck.

Actually: "When you gesture, Mute receives it." And I receive speech? No — "You never receive speech." I am Deaf, so I hear nothing. But can I see gestures? The Deaf monkey "Cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" — seeing is fine. Gestures are visual, so I should receive gestures. Let me reconsider the channels: Mute can't speak but can gesture. Blind can't see gestures. So Mute's only output that reaches anyone is gestures to me (Deaf), since Blind can't see and Deaf... I can see gestures.

So the loop: Mute reads manual → gestures the rule to me → I speak the rule aloud to Blind → Blind acts. That's the only path. I must be ready to receive Mute's gestures and relay them.

For now, I have nothing from anyone yet. I should announce what I see so Mute (who hears me) and Blind (who hears me) both know the bomb's appearance. Blind especially needs my description since they can't see.

Let me send my observation to both, and gesture nothing yet since I have no rule to relay.

I'll speak to everyone (Mute and Blind both hear me) describing the bomb. I'll also specifically address Blind since they need the physical description to act.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb reads: display shows 1, light is orange. Seven wires left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Mute, read the manual and gesture the rule to me — I will relay it to Blind. Blind, hold on, rule incoming.")
speak(to="blind", text="For your hands: wires in order are white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green. Display is 1. Light is orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Let me parse what arrived.

**Mute gestures to Deaf:** seven ✊ (fist) symbols. Seven fists — that matches seven wires. But a fist is just a shape; it has no inherent meaning. Mute is telling me something about the wires, but the symbols alone don't encode which wire or what action. Seven identical fists... Hmm. Could mean "all wires" or could be a count. Without a shared code, a fist means nothing yet.

**Blind gestures to Deaf:** 👍 ✋ — thumbs up, then an open hand. Again, no established meaning. Blind can't read the manual, so Blind is probably signaling readiness or asking something. 👍 could mean "ok/ready," ✋ could mean "stop/wait" or "I have five" or just a hand.

The problem: gestures carry symbols, but a symbol means nothing until somebody makes it mean something. We haven't agreed on any code. Mute is trying to convey the manual's rule but I have no key to decode seven fists.

Wait — maybe Mute is spelling. There's no letter alphabet given, only these emoji. So Mute can't spell words. Mute can only gesture symbols, and I receive them as symbols. The manual presumably gives a rule referencing wire colours/positions. Mute needs a way to say "cut the Nth wire" or "cut the wire of colour X."

Seven fists = seven wires? Maybe Mute is saying "the rule concerns the wires" or "there are seven." Or maybe Mute is counting positions and the fist means "this one" — but all seven are fists, so no distinction.

I think the real issue: we need an agreed encoding. I should propose one. Since I can speak (Mute and Blind hear me), I can propose a code that Mute then uses via gestures. But Blind can't hear gestures and can't see — Blind only hears my speech. So ultimately I must translate everything into speech for Blind.

Let me propose: Mute gestures a number of fingers to indicate wire position, or uses a symbol per colour. Actually simpler: I'll ask Mute to gesture the wire's position using a count, and the action using 👍 (cut) or 👎 (don't cut). But Mute's seven fists might already be an answer.

Alternatively, maybe Mute is indicating the answer is "all of them" or the rule is about the whole set. But cutting all wires is surely wrong.

Let me think about what a manual rule with display=1, light=orange might be. Common bomb rules: "if display is 1, cut the first wire," or "if light is orange, cut the wire whose colour is..." I can't know without the manual.

Best move: establish a code and ask Mute to re-send. I'll define: gesture the position number as that many fingers? But symbols are fixed emoji, not finger counts. Hmm, the alphabet has 👆 (one finger up), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three?), ✋ (five/open hand), ✊ (fist/zero?). Not clean.

Actually maybe: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4? ✋=5, and so on. But that's a stretch.

Let me reconsider: Mute sent seven ✊. Perhaps Mute is saying "the answer involves all wires" or "I can't encode it." Blind sent 👍 ✋ — maybe "yes, five"? Or Blind is confirming readiness.

I think the productive step is to propose an explicit code and ask Mute to use it. I'll define a simple scheme: use 👆 for wire 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 🖖 for 4, ✋ for 5, 🤙 for 6, 🤘 for 7 — no, too arbitrary and Mute can't confirm.

Better: I'll propose that Mute gesture the wire NUMBER as repeated 👆 (one finger) — e.g., three 👆 = wire 3 — and then 👍 to cut or 👎 to not cut. And ask Mute to confirm the code with 👍. Also tell Blind to wait.

Actually, I realize I should just ask Mute directly and give a clear, simple protocol. Let me also acknowledge Blind.

Let me send: to Mute, propose the code and ask for the rule. To Blind, tell them to wait for my instruction.

I'll speak (both hear) and also gesture to Mute (only Mute sees gestures) — but Mute CAN hear my speech, so speaking suffices for Mute. Gestures are only needed if Mute couldn't hear, but Mute can hear. Wait — Mute "Cannot speak" but can hear. So Mute hears me. Good. So I don't need to gesture to Mute at all; I can just speak.

But Mute cannot speak — Mute can only gesture. And gestures reach only me (Deaf). So Mute→me via gesture, me→everyone via speech. Confirmed chain.

So I'll speak to establish the code, and Mute will gesture back the rule.

Let me write it.

```
speak(text="Mute, I got seven fists — no meaning yet, we have no shared code. Let's set one. To give me a wire number, gesture that many 👆 (one finger). To say CUT gesture 👍 after the number; to say DO NOT CUT gesture 👎. Example: wire 3 cut = 👆👆👆👍. Please confirm you understand by gesturing 👍 alone. Then send the rule.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold. I am decoding the manual from Mute. Do not touch anything yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Let me decode.

**Mute gestures:** first 👍 alone — confirms Mute understood my code. Then 👆👆👆👆👆👆👆👍 — seven one-fingers followed by thumbs up. By my code, seven 👆 = wire 7, then 👍 = CUT. So the rule says **cut wire 7**.

Wait, but let me double check my own code: "gesture that many 👆 to give the wire number." Seven 👆 = wire 7. Then 👍 = cut. So Mute is saying: cut wire 7.

Wire 7 is **green**.

But hold on — earlier Mute sent seven ✊ (fists), not seven 👆. Now Mute sends seven 👆. The switch from ✊ to 👆 is meaningful: Mute adapted to my code. Good, that increases my confidence this is a genuine encoded answer: wire 7, cut.

**Blind gestures:** 👍 ✋ again — same as before. 👍 likely "ready/ok," ✋ maybe "waiting" or "five." Blind is just signaling readiness. Blind can't see gestures anyway, so Blind gesturing is odd — Blind can't see to make meaningful gestures? Actually Blind can still move hands; gestures are received by whoever can see. I (Deaf) can see, so I receive Blind's gestures. Blind is signaling readiness to me.

So my job: relay to Blind (who hears my speech) the instruction: cut wire 7, which is green.

But wait — I should sanity-check. Is it possible Mute meant something else? Seven 👆 could also be "wire 7." The 👍 after confirms cut. I'm fairly confident.

However, let me reconsider whether the code is unambiguous. My code said "gesture that many 👆." Mute did exactly that. Good.

One concern: could seven 👆 mean "seven wires" generally rather than wire 7? But then the trailing 👍 (cut) would be ambiguous. Given my protocol, seven 👆 = position 7. I'll go with cut wire 7.

Now, Blind can't see, so Blind needs to know which wire to cut by position and/or colour. Blind can feel the wires. Does Blind know colours? Blind "Cannot see a colour." So Blind can only identify wires by position/order or texture. I should tell Blind: cut the 7th wire from the left (the last one), which is green. Blind can count positions by feel.

Let me instruct Blind clearly, and also confirm to Mute.

Actually, I should be careful: Blind needs to locate wire 7. If Blind can count wires by position, "the last wire, seventh from the left" works. Let me give both position and colour.

Let me send.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Rule decoded: CUT wire 7 — the seventh from the left, the last one. Its colour is green. Count to the seventh wire and cut it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded: cut wire 7 (green). Relaying to Blind now. Confirm if that matches the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟 ✊]

The bomb changed. New state:

- DISPLAY now shows **8**
- LIGHT now **blue**
- Wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 CUT (green, already cut)

**Mute gestures:** 👍 — just "ok/confirmed." No new rule yet.

**Blind gestures:** ✌ 🤟 ✊ — two, three, fist. Hmm. By my own code, ✌ isn't defined (I defined 👆 for counting). Blind can't read the manual, so Blind isn't giving a rule. ✌🤟✊ = 2, 3, 0? Or Blind is just making hand shapes with no code — meaningless until defined. Blind might be trying to communicate something but we have no shared code with Blind. Blind can't see gestures either, so Blind making gestures is only for me (I can see). But Blind doesn't know my code.

Actually — important realization: Blind CAN hear my speech. And Blind can gesture. So Blind and I can communicate: I speak (Blind hears), Blind gestures (I see). We could set up a code too. But Blind holds no manual, so Blind has no rule to give. Blind's gestures are probably just acknowledgments or attempts.

✌🤟✊: two-three-zero? Or "2, 3, ?" Maybe Blind is trying to say something about wires? Or maybe Blind is confused.

The key now: I need the NEW rule for the new bomb state (display 8, light blue). Mute must read the manual again and gesture the new rule.

I should ask Mute for the new rule, and tell Blind to wait.

Let me also note: the manual presumably has rules keyed to display/light. Mute needs to read it fresh.

Let me send.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb: display 8, light blue. Wire 7 is already cut. Read the manual for this state and gesture the new rule using our code: number of 👆 = wire position, then 👍 to cut or 👎 to not cut. If the rule is not about a single wire, tell me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Good work, wire 7 was correct. New bomb now: display 8, light blue. Hold, decoding new rule.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Mute gestures:** 🤲 — open palms / cupped hands. That's not in my code. It's not 👆 repeated, not 👍, not 👎. So Mute is signaling something outside the wire-number code. Maybe 🤲 means "I can't express it" or "the rule is different" or "open/all" or "give me something."

**Blind gestures:** 👍 — ready/ok.

Hmm. Mute sent a single 🤲. This is ambiguous. It could mean:
- "The rule isn't a simple wire cut" 
- "The answer is all wires" (open palms = all?)
- "I don't understand / need a different code"
- Something about the manual's structure.

I need to disambiguate. Let me ask Mute directly with yes/no questions I can decode. I'll propose: gesture 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. Then ask specific questions.

Possible questions:
1. Is the rule about cutting a single wire? (👍/👎)
2. Is the rule about cutting multiple wires?
3. Does the rule depend on the light colour?
4. Does the rule depend on the display number?

But Mute can only gesture, and I can only give yes/no. Let me structure a few questions.

Actually, maybe 🤲 means "the rule involves the whole set / all wires" or "open the bomb"? Or maybe Mute is saying the manual's rule for this state is "cut all wires"? That seems dangerous.

Let me ask clearly. I'll define 👍=yes, 👎=no, and ask: "Is the rule a single wire cut?" If no, ask more.

Also I should relay to Blind to hold.

Let me send.

```
speak(to="mute", text="🤲 received but not in our code. Let's use 👍=yes, 👎=no. Question 1: Is the required action cutting exactly one wire? Answer 👍 or 👎. If yes, send the wire number as 👆 repeats then 👍.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still decoding. Hold, do not touch anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

**Mute gestures:** 👍 then 🤲.

👍 = yes to my question "Is the required action cutting exactly one wire?" So yes, it's a single wire cut.

Then 🤲 again. Hmm. So Mute confirms it's a single wire cut, but then sends 🤲 again. Maybe 🤲 is Mute's way of giving the wire number, or Mute is stuck on how to express the position.

Wait — maybe 🤲 means "the wire I mean is..." no. Or maybe Mute is saying the wire number in a different way. 🤲 = two cupped hands, could represent... 2? Or "both hands" = 10? Or maybe it's a colour indicator?

Alternatively, maybe Mute can't express the wire number with 👆 because... no, Mute used 👆 before.

Let me reconsider. Maybe 🤲 represents a specific wire by some property. Or maybe Mute is indicating the wire is the one that's... hmm.

Let me just ask directly: "Send the wire number as repeated 👆." If Mute sends 👆 repeats, great.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, single wire cut confirmed. Please send the wire number as repeated 👆 (one finger), then 👍. If 🤲 was meant as the number, tell me: does 🤲 mean a number? 👍/👎.")

```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

**Mute gestures:** 👎 then 🤲.

👎 = no to "does 🤲 mean a number?" So 🤲 is not a number. But Mute keeps sending 🤲 and won't send 👆 repeats. So Mute cannot or will not express the wire number via my 👆 code.

Why? Maybe because the wire to cut is already cut (wire 7), so there's no valid single wire? But Mute said yes it's a single wire cut.

Or maybe 🤲 means something like "the wire is the one you must identify by a property, not a position" — like "the wire matching the light colour" or "the wire matching the display."

Maybe 🤲 represents a colour? Like "blue" (the light is blue)? Or maybe Mute is pointing to a wire by colour and 🤲 is a colour gesture.

```
speak(to="mute", text="🤲 is not a number, got it. Let's pin it with yes/no. Q1: Is the wire to cut the same colour as the light (blue)? 👍/👎. Q2: Is it wire 1? Q3: wire 2? Q4: wire 3? Q5: wire 4? Q6: wire 5? Q7: wire 6? Answer each with 👍 or 👎 in order.")
```
